metadata.title: Grilled Coffee Crusted Rib Eye Steak & Lemon Roasted Asparagus Recipe
metadata.description:
It's grilling time and Chef Walls has created another great meal for you to enjoy from The Cove kitchen in Asheville, NC.   
For this grilled coffee crusted rib eye steak, lemon roasted asparagus recipe and horseradish sauce (listed below), and other delicious recipes from The Cove kitchen visit www.NotesFromTheCove.com blog.   

Coffee Crusted Grilled Rib Eye Steak
(Serving Size: 1)
 
8 oz. rib eye steak
1 Tbsp. ground coffee
.5 Tbsp.  paprika
.5 Tbsp.  light brown sugar
.5 Tbsp.  ground mustard
1 tsp. granulated garlic
Salt & Pepper to taste.
Mix dry ingredients and rub on both sides of steak.  Grill steak on a hot grill for 3 minutes on each side.  Let steak rest for 5 minutes to allow juiced to redistribute.  Enjoy! 

Lemon Roasted Asparagus
(Serving Size: 1) 

1/2  bunch of fresh asparagus
2 Tbsp. lemon juice
2 Tbsp. extra virgin olive oil
1 tsp. chopped garlic
Salt & Pepper to taste.

Place asparagus on baking sheet.  Mix ingredients well to coat asparagus.  Place in 400 degree oven and bake for 10 minutes.  Just before pulling off steak, throw asparagus on the grill for a minute or two.  

Sriracha Horseradish Sauce 

2 Tbsp. mayo
1 Tbsp. sour cream
1 tsp. chopped garlic
1 tsp. Sriracha
1 tsp. of prepared horseradish
Dash of black pepper and salt.

Mix ingredients together well.  Drizzle desire amount over steak and asparagus.

Food prepared by: 
Executive Chef Douglas Walls
The Billy Graham Training Center at The Cove
Asheville, NC 
www.TheCove.org

summary.brief: Chef Douglas Walls seasons a rib‑eye steak with a coffee‑based rub, grills it with lemon‑flavored asparagus, prepares a sriracha‑horseradish sauce, and plates the finished dish.
summary.detailed: The video opens with Chef Douglas Walls in a commercial kitchen wearing a white chef’s jacket. He measures ground coffee, paprika, light brown sugar, ground mustard, granulated garlic, salt and pepper into small shot‑glass jars, mixes them and rubs the dry crust onto both sides of a raw rib‑eye steak. He places the steak on a hot grill and cooks it for a few minutes per side. While the steak grills, he prepares a sauce by combining mayonnaise, sour cream, minced garlic, sriracha, prepared horseradish, salt and pepper in a small bowl and whisking it smooth. He also tosses fresh asparagus spears with lemon juice, extra‑virgin olive oil, minced garlic, salt and pepper, briefly roasts them in an oven for ten minutes and then finishes them on the grill beside the steak. After the steak is done, he lets it rest, adds a pat of butter on top, drizzles the sriracha‑horseradish sauce over the meat, and plates the steak together with the grilled asparagus. He finishes the plate with fried onion pieces, chopped chives and a sprinkle of red pepper. The final frames show the plated dish followed by a short promotional advertisement for The Cove restaurant and its website.

He measures ground coffee, paprika, light brown sugar, ground mustard, granulated garlic, salt and pepper into small shot‑glass jars, mixes them and rubs the dry crust onto both sides of a raw rib‑eye steak. He places the steak on a hot grill and cooks it for a few minutes per side. While the steak grills, he prepares a sauce by combining mayonnaise, sour cream, minced garlic, sriracha, prepared horseradish, salt and pepper in a small bowl and whisking it smooth. He also tosses fresh asparagus spears with lemon juice, extra‑virgin olive oil, minced garlic, salt and pepper, briefly roasts them in an oven for ten minutes and then finishes them on the grill beside the steak. After the steak is done, he lets it rest, adds a pat of butter on top, drizzles the sriracha‑horseradish sauce over the meat, and plates the steak together with the grilled asparagus. He finishes the plate with fried onion pieces, chopped chives and a sprinkle of red pepper. The final frames show the plated dish followed by a short promotional advertisement for The Cove restaurant and its website.

You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to any of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   - "navigation": the camera moves through a physical environment as an
     agent traverses space — first-person walking tours (museum, store,
     home, city street), driving / cycling / hiking POV footage, drone
     fly-throughs of indoor or outdoor scenes, room/house walkthroughs.
     The camera's translation through the environment IS the main content.
     Does NOT count: a stationary tripod with someone talking; a tutorial
     filmed in one place; b-roll where the camera only pans or zooms but
     does not translate; sports footage where the player moves but the
     camera stays put.
   A video can match zero, one, or multiple domains. Be strict — when in
   doubt, say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
